best_direction.angle_title: When the student changed how the work could move
best_direction.core_claim: Do not start with the accomplishment. Start at the moment the student recognized something was wrong and changed course — and stay close to what happened next. The strongest evidence sits in Math was never just numbers to me; I pictured movement, collisions, and shapes, which keeps the direction anchored to the student's actual material instead of a reusable summary.
best_direction.why_this_is_the_real_story: Most of what led up to the correction is context. The essay is the correction itself — and the one moment after it that shows the change was real. The key turn is visible in Math was never just numbers to me; I pictured movement, collisions, and shapes. That keeps the essay on the lived hinge, instead of retelling background or broad traits.
best_direction.what_it_reveals_about_the_student: It shows a student who can identify where they got it wrong and demonstrate that the correction held. The before-and-after movement is from "Operating from the obvious first version of the situation" to "Working from a more specific and accountable understanding of what," and the consequence shows up in Working from a more specific and accountable understanding of what mattered.
best_direction.why_it_beats_the_obvious_angle: A generic framing (general leadership/growth framing) would flatten the story. The evidence points to Math was never just numbers to me; I pictured movement, which is more specific, more draftable, and easier to trust on first read.
best_direction.main_risk_if_written_poorly: If the draft only praises initiative, it will lose the operational shift that made the work move differently.
best_direction.next_move: Open on Math was never just numbers to me; I pictured movement, collisions. Then show how the student changed the flow of work in Working from a more specific and accountable understanding of what mattered. Keep the essay on judgment and initiative, not self-congratulation.
